text:
At the foot of distant mountains lay a small village. A young farmer named Karim lived there. He was poor, and his plot of land was tiny, but his heart was full of big dreams. Every day he told himself: “One day, I will own the tallest and strongest tree in this village.”

One day at the market, Karim met a traveling merchant. The merchant showed him a small brown seed and said, “This is a bamboo seed. I brought it from a faraway land. If you are patient, it will change your life.”

Karim took the seed home. He planted it in the best spot in his yard and watered it. His neighbors grew curious too, and they planted all kinds of things in their own plots: fast-growing greens and young fruit saplings.

After a week, the neighbors’ plants were sprouting. After two weeks, they were already reaching upward, a joy to look at. But Karim’s patch of earth stayed empty. Not a single leaf.

A month passed. Nothing. Two months passed. Still nothing. The neighbors began to laugh. “Karim, you must have planted a stone!” they said. “You’re wasting your effort. That seed is dead!”

Karim said nothing. Every morning he got up and watered the spot where the seed was buried. He loosened the soil, pulled the weeds, and added fertilizer. In the evening he came back and looked at the ground again.

The first year passed. The neighbors’ trees were now waist-high. Karim’s patch was still bare. People mocked him openly now: “Behold Karim’s garden! The only thing that grows here is dirt!”

Doubt crept into Karim’s heart. At night, lying in bed, he thought: “What if they’re right? What if I’m wasting my time? What if the merchant lied to me?” But in the morning, he picked up his bucket and walked to his land again. Because he understood one thing: if he stopped, he would never know.

The second year passed. No result. The third year. The fourth. The neighbors’ trees grew large and gave shade. They sat beneath them, looked at Karim’s land, and shook their heads. “Poor Karim. Even if he were the best farmer in the world, what could come from one seed?”

Even his friends began to advise him: “Don’t ruin your land. Plant something else. Four years have passed and nothing has come up. It never will.”

Karim listened quietly. Then he said, “I planted the seed. That was my part. The rest, it knows by itself.” And he went back to watering.

Spring of the fifth year arrived. One morning Karim approached his land and couldn’t believe his eyes. A tiny green shoot was peeking out of the soil!

Karim fell to his knees and wept. That whole day he sat beside the shoot, guarding it like a fortress.

And then something incredible happened. The shoot began to grow. On the first day, a hand’s width. On the second, even taller. Within a week it was as tall as a man. Within two weeks it rose above the roof of his house. By the sixth week, the bamboo had climbed thirty meters into the sky. It was the tallest tree in the whole village.

The neighbors ran over with their mouths hanging open. “What miracle is this?!” they said. “For five years there was nothing, and now it’s grown thirty meters in a month?”

Then an old gardener dug into the soil and stood stunned. “Look,” he said. “This seed didn’t stand still for five years. All that time it was sending roots underground. They’ve spread in every direction, hundreds of meters. Now no storm can ever knock it down.”

And so it was. For five whole years, the bamboo had been doing invisible but vital work: building a strong foundation. And once the foundation was ready, it shot into the sky in an instant.

Karim lifted his head, looked at the tall bamboo, and smiled. Now he knew one thing: patience doesn’t waste time. It builds it.

Moral: Sometimes you are growing, but nobody sees it, not even you. Not seeing results doesn’t mean nothing is changing. The deepest roots take the longest to grow. Be patient, keep working, because when your time comes, nothing will be able to stop you

tr.title: Bambuk daraxti
paragraphs: Uzoq tog’lar etagida kichik bir qishloq bor ekan. Qishloqda Karim ismli yosh dehqon yashar ekan. U kambag’al, yeri ham kichkina ekan, lekin ko’ngli katta orzularga to’la ekan. Har kuni o’ziga o’zi: «Bir kun kelib, men ham shu qishloqdagi eng baland va eng baquvvat daraxtning egasi bo’laman», derkan.

Bir kuni Karim bozorda yo’lovchi savdogarni uchratibdi. Savdogar unga kichkina, jigarrang bir urug’ni ko’rsatib debdi: «Bu bambuk urug’i. Uzoq mamlakatdan olib kelganman. Agar sabr qilsang, u sening hayotingni o’zgartiradi.»

Karim urug’ni olib, uyiga qaytibdi. Hovlisining eng yaxshi yeriga ekib, ustiga suv quyibdi. Qo’shnilari ham qiziqib, o’z yerlariga turli o’simliklar ekishibdi. Ular tezda o’sadigan ko’katlar, mevali nihollar ekishgan ekan.
Bir haftadan keyin qo’shnilarning ekinlari ko’karib chiqibdi. Ikki haftadan keyin ular allaqachon bo’y cho’zib, ko’zni quvontiribdi. Karimning yeri esa bo’m-bo’sh turaveribdi. Birorta ham novda yo’q.
Bir oy o’tibdi. Hech narsa yo’q. Ikki oy o’tibdi. Yana hech narsa. Qo’shnilar kula boshlabdi. «Karim, yeringda tosh ekkan bo’lsang kerak!» deyishibdi. «Bekor mehnat qilyapsan, bu urug’ o’lgan!»
Karim indamabdi. Har kuni ertalab turib, urug’ ekilgan yerni sug’oribdi. Tuproqni yumshatibdi, begona o’tlarni yulibdi, o’g’it solibdi. Kech kirganda yana kelib, tuproqqa qarab qo’yibdi.
Birinchi yil o’tibdi. Qo’shnilarning daraxtlari endi belga yetibdi. Karimning yeri esa hamon bo’m-bo’sh. Odamlar endi ochiq masxara qilishibdi: «Mana, Karimning bog’i! Bu yerda faqat tuproq o’sadi!»

Karimning ichiga shubha kirib qolibdi. Kechasi yotganda o’ylabdi: «Balki ular haq? Balki men vaqtimni bekor sarflayotgandirman? Balki savdogar meni aldagandir?» Lekin ertalab turganda yana qo’lida chelak bilan yerga yo’l olibdi. Chunki u bir narsani tushungan ekan: agar to’xtasa, hech qachon bilmaydi.

Ikkinchi yil o’tibdi. Natija yo’q. Uchinchi yil ham. To’rtinchi yil ham. Qo’shnilarning daraxtlari endi katta bo’lib, soya tashlay boshlabdi. Ular daraxt tagida o’tirib, Karimning yeriga qarab, bosh chayqashibdi. «Bechora Karim. Dunyodagi eng yaxshi dehqon bo’lsa ham, urug’dan nima chiqadi?»
Hatto Karimning do’stlari ham unga maslahat bera boshlabdi: «Yeringni bekor qilma. Boshqa narsa ek. To’rt yil bo’ldi, hech narsa chiqmadi, endi chiqmaydi.»
Karim jimgina eshitibdi. Keyin debdi: «Men urug’ni ekdim. Bu mening vazifam edi. Qolganini esa u o’zi biladi.» Va yana sug’orishga ketibdi.
Beshinchi yilning bahori kelibdi. Bir tong Karim yerga yaqinlashib, ko’zlariga ishonmabdi. Tuproqdan kichkina yashil novda boshini ko’tarib turgan ekan!
Karim tiz cho’kib, yig’lab yuboribdi. Shu kuni u o’z yerida kichkina yashil novdani qo’rg’ondek himoya qilib o’tiribdi.

Va keyin g’alati voqea yuz beribdi. Novda kundan-kunga o’sa boshlabdi. Birinchi kuni bir qarich. Ikkinchi kuni undan ham uzun. Bir hafta ichida odam bo’yiga yetibdi. Ikki hafta ichida uyning tomidan oshib ketibdi. Oltinchi haftaga kelib, bambuk o’ttiz metr balandlikka ko’tarilibdi. Butun qishloqdagi eng baland daraxt bo’libdi.
Qo’shnilar hayratdan og’izlari ochilib, yig’ilib kelishibdi. «Bu qanday mo’’jiza?!» deyishibdi. «Besh yil hech narsa chiqmagan edi, endi bir oyda o’ttiz metr bo’ldi?»

Shunda keksa bir bog’bon tuproqni qazib ko’ribdi va og’zi ochilib qolibdi. «Qarang», debdi u. «Bu urug’ besh yil o’smagan emas. U besh yil davomida yer ostida ildiz otib turgan. Uning ildizlari bu yerda hamma yo’nalishda, yuzlab metrga yoyilgan. Endi u hech qanday bo’ronda qulamaydi.»
Aslida shunday ekan. Bambuk besh yil davomida ko’zga ko’rinmas, ammo muhim ish qilgan ekan: mustahkam poydevor qurgan ekan. Va poydevor tayyor bo’lgach, u bir zumda osmonga ko’tarilibdi.
Karim esa boshini ko’tarib, baland bambukka qarabdi va jilmayibdi. Endi u bir narsani bilar ekan: sabr tufayli yo’qotilgan vaqt yo’q.

Qissadan hissa: Ba’zida sen o’sib turasan, lekin hech kim ko’rmaydi, hatto sen ham. Natija ko’rinmayotgani, hech narsa o’zgarmayotganini anglatmaydi. Eng chuqur ildizlar eng ko’p vaqt oladi. Sabr qil, mehnatingni davom ettir, chunki sening vaqting kelganda, hech narsa seni to’xtata olmaydi.

quiz.q: Karim's bamboo grew quickly in the first year.
The bamboo was growing roots underground for five years.
What did the neighbors say about Karim's seed?
o: That it was dead or a stone
That it was a magic seed
That they wanted to buy it
